articles.title: Previewing New England’s Week 9 Matchup vs. the Green Bay Packers | Patriots Roundtable Podcast
articles.summary: The New England Patriots return home for a prolific matchup against the Green Bay Packers at Gillette Stadium on Sunday evening. We preview the game on today...
articles.body:
Check out the Patriots Roundtable Podcast for more!

This Sunday, the New England Patriots (5-3) return to the comfort of Gillette Stadium for one of their most premier matchups of the 2026 regular season: an interconference showdown with the Green Bay Packers (5-3). New England's second game against NFC North opponents this fall is ripe with intrigue on the field and on the sidelines, setting up for one of the most entertaining bouts of the year league-wide.

On today's episode of the Patriots Roundtable Podcast, hosts Eddie Marotta and Tyler Geis preview the Patriots' upcoming home stand against Green Bay — examining matchups that could swing the game's result, keys to victory on both sides of the football, and predicting the game's outcome.

On the sidelines, all eyes will be fixed on two New England legends. Tom Brady makes his return to Foxboro on the FOX broadcast, and Rob Gronkowski will be inducted into the Patriots' Hall of Fame as part of the weekend's festivities.

Between the white lines, Sunday's matchup pits two teams with eerily similar identities against each other. Drake Maye and Jordan Love are both quarterbacks who have excelled at threatening defenses with downfield passing, while each team's defensive structure is built upon taking away those opportunities for their opponents.

For New England's offense, it will be another in a string of games where the health of key skill position players will be closely monitored. A.J. Brown and TreVeyon Henderson have continued to miss practice time, and have now been joined by Hunter Henry — who was limited to just eight offensive snaps before suffering a foot injury in Week 8. Those absences didn't seem to matter much for Maye and the passing attack, however, as the third-year gunslinger continued his recent excellence with another efficient performance that featured two 40-yard passing touchdowns. He'll need to carry that success over into this weekend, while the offense as a whole will look to limit the turnovers that have plagued them against a defense that leads the league in takeaways.

On the defensive side of the football, the Patriots' secondary will be challenged by an equally aggressive passing offense. Love leads all quarterbacks with 52 attempts on passes 20-plus yards downfield, and has the tools along the boundary to create explosive plays in an instant. Christian Watson, Matthew Golden, and Tucker Kraft each present stylistically different predicaments for New England's coaching staff to gameplan for, but that's been a strength so far this season. Much like the Patriots, the Packers have struggled to find consistency on the ground — ranking at or near the bottom of the league in nearly every rushing statistical or analytical category.

This will be a game that places a heavy emphasis on quarterback play on both sides — strategies that have served both teams well through eight weeks of the regular season. Who remains standing by the end of the evening could come down to one final possession, or who can force the opposition into critical mistakes. For New England, they'll look to create those errors, rather than being forced to overcome them — an internal battle that's yet to be resolved.

articles.title: Ben James produces another low round and takes the 36-hole lead in Mexico
articles.summary: Ben James posted another sub-65 round to grab the 36-hole lead by one shot at El Cardonal.
articles.body:
LOS CABOS, Mexico — Ben James ran off five straight birdies around the turn and finished with an aggressive tee shot for one last birdie and an 8-under 64 on Friday to build a one-shot lead going into the weekend at the World Wide Technology Championship.

James, already assured his PGA Tour card for next year as the No. 1 player in the PGA Tour University ranking, had his 14th round of 65 or lower in 13 tournaments since turning pro out of Virginia this summer.

He already has four finishes in the top 5 and picking up plenty of experience along the way. A victory would put him on the Championship Series under the new model in 2028 and move him into the top 50 in the world.

"It's weird, in college I was kind of someone that would shoot 2, 3 under every time out and would have trouble going low," James said. "But you adapt to your surroundings as humans, so I guess out here that's what you have to do. I've been rolling it well and playing well, so nice to be shooting some low numbers."

James was at 15-under 129 at the Tiger Woods-designed El Cardonal at Diamante. He was one shot ahead of Peter Malnati, who was tied for the lead until coming up short of the green on the par-3 ninth and missing a 12-foot par putt to end his round of 64.

"I work really hard on my game and I haven't had tons to show for that lately," Malnati said. "So to not be in that position coming down the stretch on a Friday where ... I don't even have to think about the cut line, I can think about playing golf. That was fun."

Zac Blair had a 68 and was three shots behind.

This is the second time James has had the lead going into the weekend. The other was the RBC Canadian Open, and he shot a 78 to quickly spiral out of contention. He also had a good chance to win the Biltmore Championship Asheville until Jacob Bridgeman put on a putting clinic down the stretch in the final round.

"I'm doing everything right," James said. "But for me, I'm just trying to win each shot, just do the best I can for each golf shot and not thinking ahead and just do the best I can. And as I say, winning the shot at hand."

He won the par-5 18th when he least expected it. James has been relying on his short wedges, and hit a pedestrian pitch to about 18 feet. But he holed the putt, and then started the front nine with three straight birdies to set the target.

This is among the last three tournaments of the FedEx Cup Fall, after which the top 100 players keep full status for next year.

articles.title: Tiger Woods and ex-wife Elin Nordegren reunite to celebrate son Charlie's college golf commitment
articles.summary: Tiger Woods and ex-wife Elin Nordegren reunited at their son Charlie Woods' high school to celebrate his Florida State University golf commitment.
articles.body: It was a family reunion for Charlie Woods on Friday, as both his father and mother, whose divorce was highly publicized, were together again to celebrate his college commitment. Woods, the son of 15-time major winner Tiger, announced earlier this year his commitment to play golf at Florida State University. The Woods family, including Tiger's ex-wife, Elin Nordegren, were on hand at Charlie's high school to celebrate. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Tiger and Elin got divorced after the former's infidelity had been exposed. Charlie announced the commitment in February. "Excited to announce my commitment to play golf at Florida State University — go Noles!" he wrote. "Congratulations Charlie. I'm so proud of you on entering this next chapter of your life," Tiger commented. It is a rare public appearance for Tiger, who has remained out of the spotlight most of the time since he was arrested in March. LIV GOLF IS OFFICIALLY OVER AFTER ANNOUNCING PLANS TO 'WIND-DOWN' OPERATIONS AFTER FAILED RESCUE DEAL He was arrested on charges of DUI following a car crash in which police later found hydrocodone pills in his pocket. Law enforcement proceeded to perform field sobriety tests because of their suspicions. Woods was instructed to remove his eyeglasses, and the deputy conducting the tests stated that his eyes appeared to be "bloodshot and glassy" and "extremely dilated." articles.title: Two main parties neck and neck after New Zealand vote, early count
articles.summary: Early results suggests New Zealand’s National and Labour parties polling just short of 30 percent of the popular vote.
articles.body:
New Zealand’s ruling centre-right National Party and main opposition Labour have both secured just short of 30 percent of the popular vote, with just 27 percent of the election results counted.

The Electoral Commission on Saturday showed the current three-party ruling coalition led by National would have a majority of just one seat, after an election dominated by a struggling economy and voter disillusionment with the two biggest contenders.

It added that the centrist Opportunity Party will meet the 5 percent threshold to enter parliament, potentially becoming a kingmaker.

Polling stations opened at 9am on Saturday (20:00 GMT Friday) and closed at 7pm (06:00 GMT Saturday).

New Zealand’s Electoral Commission aims to release preliminary results from 95 percent of polling stations by the end of election night on Saturday. A final result, which will reflect ballots cast by New Zealanders abroad, is expected by November 27.

There is no timeframe for when a government must be formed.

New Zealand’s 2026 election has been at times dubbed the “supermarket election”, where grocery prices and supermarket competition have become a key battleground for political parties.

Peter Dunne, a former member of New Zealand’s parliament, who also served as a minister in both National and Labour-led governments, said that the election is “much more of a cost-of-living election”, with voters essentially looking at “which of the main blocs is better placed to ease the cost of living burden on New Zealanders”.

“The ruling coalition appears well ahead of the centre-left. Now, that may change because these are early results, but it’s a little bit of a surprise that this is happening,” Dunne told Al Jazeera. “We were looking to a much tighter contest than appears to be the case at the moment.”

The National Party pledged to return the budget to surplus through fiscal discipline while expanding the national pension scheme. The Labour Party promised cheaper healthcare and transport.

The former minister added that both main parties are practically “carbon copies of the other”, leaving “a whole rising generation of voters, who want to see a bit more adventure in politics”.

Dunne said that, therefore, the results show support rallying behind other parties, like “strong support for the Green Party, the right-wing libertarian [ACT New Zealand], the xenophobic nationalist [New Zealand First] party, and a new centrist party, the Opportunity Party, which wants to be in the middle between all of them”.

He told Al Jazeera that even though the Opportunity Party is currently hovering around 5 percent at the moment – also the threshold for representation in parliament – “it’s been one of the big stars of this campaign”.

New Zealand holds a general election every three years under a mixed-member proportional system.

Voters do not elect a leader of the country, but instead select a local electorate candidate and a political party.

Dunne told Al Jazeera that if both main parties of the blocs “end up relatively evenly placed, then the onus could go on the Opportunity Party”.

“If Opportunity Party reaches parliament, it will talk to the largest party first, which appears to be the National Party, but there’s no guarantee that they could come to an arrangement,” he said.

“We could face weeks of interparty negotiations to form a government. Parliament has to sit by early January, so there’s a real prospect that we could go into Christmas with no clear government in New Zealand,” Dunne added.

Electorate winners earn a seat in the typically 120-seat parliament, as do the highest-ranked members of the party, based on their national party vote.

All votes are counted by hand, not by machine.

articles.title: Jon Rahm leads Abu Dhabi Championship with Rory McIlroy among challengers going into final round
articles.summary: John Rahm leads on 18 under, one clear of Tyrell Hatton and Francesco Laporta in tie for second; Rory McIlroy, chasing record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai title, is 16 under; final round of Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship, live on Sky Sports Golf from 6.30am on Sunday
articles.body:
McIlroy, chasing a record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai title, and coming off the back of carding a career-high 11 birdies in his second round, had shared the lead at one stage before bogeying the par-three 17th.

McIlroy's five-under 67 also included a double-bogey six at the 10th, which interrupted a streak of seven birdies from the Northern Irishman between holes seven and 14.

Rahm sits on 18 under after a six-under 66 on Saturday at Yas Links GC, one clear of Hatton and Laporta who each carded a 67.

Adam Scott continued his bogey-free tournament with a 66 to sit 15 under in fifth place, one shot behind McIlroy.

It leaves three Masters champions in the top five of the leaderboard, with Rahm (2023), McIlroy (2025, 2026) and Scott (2013) all in the mix going into the final day.

The two-week playoffs on the DP World Tour saw 70 players enter the $9m Abu Dhabi Championship before the 50 top-ranked players advance to the $10m finals event in Dubai next week.

McIlroy is currently projected to rise to No 2 in the Road to Dubai rankings, behind Eugenio Chacarra who fired a five-under 67 on Saturday to find himself tied for 29th in Abu Dhabi at eight under.

articles.summary: El de Barrika borda el sábado y retrasa a McIlroy, que achucha al líder de la Race to Dubai
articles.body: En la economía colaborativa que este fin de semana protagoniza el deporte español, Alcaraz mete a Jódar en las Finales ATP y Jon Rahm impulsa las opciones de victoria de Eugenio López-Chacarra para ser campeón del DP World Tour la próxima semana en Dubái como sólo entre los españoles hizo él en 2019 y Seve Ballesteros en seis ocasiones. En un sábado soleado en Abu Dabi, sin viento severo y banderas para hacer resultado si se era preciso, Jon bordó el golf en los segundos nueve hoyos. Los despachó en 31 golpes, con tres birdies y un eagle -un putt de 9 metros-, para firmar un rotundo 66, uno más que horas antes había firmado Ángel Ayora, protagonista de una buena escalada en el día del movimiento, cuya recompensa final puede ser en siete días un billete para el PGA Tour. El joven de San Roque compartió con Ding la mejor vuelta del día. (Resultados) Anunció a comienzos de semana Jon, que había dedicado más tiempo a los biberones que a los hierros en este mes y medio largo, que su juego estaba oxidado, pero bastó el contacto con Yas Links, un campo que premia al que coge calle más que otros, para cogerle el pulso otra vez y plantarse a falta de 18 hoyos con 18 bajo par y con un golpe de ventaja sobre su antiguo compañero en la extinta Legión XIII, Tyrrell Hatton y el italiano Francesco Laporta. Sobre todo fue en los segundos nueve donde hizo la vuelta. Estuvo algo dubitativo en el inicio, pero supo aprovechar los dos pares 5 para paliar el bogey del hoyo 4 (par 3) porque no cogió el green. Sacarle partido a los hoyos largos, faceta que en torneos a veces le cuesta al vizcaíno, es un condicionante grande en campos como el del Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship. Aquí en tres días acumula -11 en 12 hoyos.Se le escapó por medio palmo el del 18, a la caída de la tarde, para haber ampliado más distancia. Mientras, Rory Mcilroy, que ha ganado cinco veces en el desierto, pero no en este emirato, tiró 67 golpes y es cuarto a dos de Jon. El norirlandés, el número 2 del mundo, persigue su octava Orden de Mérito ahora llamada Race to Dubái con Chacarra como principal adversario. Rory lleva 25 birdies en Abu Dhabi. Nunca había hecho tantos en el DP World Tour tras el sábado. Un doble bogey en el 10 le birló el liderato. El madrileño, mientras, olvidó los problemas con el driver que había tenido esta semana y firmó otro 67 para ascender hasta el vigésimo noveno puesto. Chacarra lamentó que algún bogey, como el del 15, se produjese después de haber pegado el segundo golpe desde el centro de la calle, pero acabó satisfecho y derrochando humildad. "Me he dado cuenta cuando jugué con Rory el jueves que hay 36 jugadores por delante de mí en el ránking y que tengo que seguir trabajando y mejorar para llegar donde está él". Si se mantienen en ese tono el domingo, el español saldrá en Dubái con unos 600 puntos sobre McIlroy. Un colchoncito sin ser nada definitivo.

articles.title: Abu Dhabi Championship: Jon Rahm takes one-shot lead into final round
articles.summary: Jon Rahm leads Tyrrell Hatton and Francesca Laporta by one shot, and Rory McIlroy by two, after the third round of the Abu Dhabi Championship.
articles.body:
Abu Dhabi Championship third-round leaderboard

18 J Rahm (Spa); -17 T Hatton (Eng), F Laporta (Ita); -16 R McIlroy (NI); -15 A Scott (Aus); -14 M Jordan (Eng), D Puig (Spa)

Selected others: -12 S Bairstow (Eng), N Kimsey (Eng); -11 T Fleetwood (Eng), E Ferguson (Sco), A Sullivan (Eng); -9 A Rai (Eng); -8 E Chacarra (Spa), M Wallace (Eng); -1 P Reed (US)

Jon Rahm has a one-shot lead going into the final round of the Abu Dhabi Championship but Ryder Cup team-mates Tyrrell Hatton and Rory McIlroy are in close contention.

The 31-year-old Spaniard shared the overnight lead with Italy's Francesco Laporta and fellow former LIV player Hatton, but moved clear of them both with a six-under-par 66 at Yas Links on Saturday.

Hatton and Laporta both carded a 67, as did McIlroy, who goes into the final round in fourth place on 16 under.

Rahm, who said recently that he does not know what 2027 holds after quitting the LIV tour, is aiming for a first solo tournament triumph since winning the Masters in 2023.

Reigning Masters champion McIlroy remains in hot pursuit, however, after bouncing back in spectacular fashion since being given a two-shot penalty in the opening round for improving his lie before taking a chip shot.

The six-time major winner hit 11 birdies in a second-round 63 and another eight in his third round, but a double bogey six at the par-four 10th - and another dropped shot at the 17th - left McIlroy two shots off the lead.

And he acknowledges that it will take something special on the final day to reel in Rahm and co.

"There are low ones [scores] out there and I am going to have to shoot a low one - something in the mid to low 60s - to get it done tomorrow and that will be the goal," said McIlroy.

Hatton, meanwhile, is looking forward to going head-to-head again with Rahm after playing alongside the two-time major champion, and Laporta, in Saturday's final group.

All three will play together once again on Sunday.

"Obviously final group tomorrow there's a lot to play for," said Hatton, who briefly moved level with Rahm at the top of the leaderboard in the third round after holing his seventh birdie of the day on the 14th.

"Naturally we are going to want to beat each other. Hopefully I can get off to a good start and put him under some pressure."

Rahm, who is chasing his first win in the Abu Dhabi Championship, responded well after being put under pressure by Hatton on Saturday.

He reclaimed the outright lead on the 15th with a superb, curling 20-foot birdie putt and came close to extending his advantage at the last, just coming up short with another birdie chance as he finished without a single dropped shot.

Laporta also produced a bogey-free round to keep pace with the field's big hitters as the 36-year-old, who shot 10 under par to claim a first-round lead, bids for a first title on the DP World Tour.

Elsewhere, Australian Adam Scott remained bogey-free for the tournament after three rounds and moved up to fifth place on 15 under with a 66.

And Englishman Matthew Jordan is a shot further back, alongside Spain's David Puig, after a third-round 69.

articles.title: Jiří Klíma's late goals not enough as Beavers fall to Bowling Green
articles.summary: Nov. 7—BOWLING GREEN, Ohio — Bowling Green had the strongest of starts and never looked back. Just 15 seconds into Friday's series opener, the Bemidji State...
articles.body:
Nov. 7—BOWLING GREEN, Ohio — Bowling Green had the strongest of starts and never looked back.

Just 15 seconds into Friday's series opener, the Bemidji State men's hockey team fell behind 1-0 when Brody Waters finished Brayden Crampton's one-time pass. Three minutes and 12 seconds later, Ty Higgins scored a shorthanded goal on a tight-angle shot to put Bowling Green ahead 2-0.

The Falcons sat on the early cushion, then padded the lead to hand the Beavers their first CCHA loss of the season, 5-2.

BGSU sat on the two-goal lead until the final minutes of the second period. Brandon Whynott tapped home a pass from Dominik Rymon with 82 seconds left before the intermission. Waters added his second goal of the night three and a half minutes into the third period.

Jiří Klíma got the Beavers back into the game with a pair of goals 49 seconds apart. He converted on BSU's sixth and final power play of the night, with assists from Max Namestnikov and Oliver Peer. Klíma then beat goaltender Jacob Steinman five-hole to pull Bemidji State within two.

Connor Levis silenced the comeback effort with his empty-net goal with 1:35 left in regulation. The Beavers fell to 2-5-1 (1-1-1 CCHA), while the Falcons (5-4) remained a perfect 3-0 in league games.

Steinman finished with 27 saves on 29 shots. Max Hildebrand stopped 20 shots for BSU. The Beavers filled off six of their seven penalties, including 38 seconds of a 5-on-3 in the second period.

articles.title: Patriots activate wideout Mack Hollins off the injury reserve
articles.summary: The New England Patriots have announced that they are activating wide receiver Mack Hollins from the injury reserve.
articles.body:
The New England Patriots have announced that they are activating wide receiver Mack Hollins from the injury reserve.

Hollins, who played the first four games of the season, had totaled 15 receptions for 209 yards. In 2025, he totaled nearly 50 receptions for over 500 yards and 2 touchdowns.

Hollins was injured back in week 4 against the Bills with a calf injury.

The Pats get an extra boost at the wide receiver position, with Hollins joining Pop Douglas, Efton Chism, and Kyle Williams, with A.J. Brown ruled out another week due to a lingering knee issue and Romeo Doubs also on injured reserve.

New England hosts the Green Bay Packers at Foxborough tomorrow at 4:25 PM.
